what: DERIVATION, independent attempt 1 of 4: When is a body's capture rate proportional to its number of records?. SETTING (blocks 44 and 45; open PRs titled 'ail44: records with inertia' and 'ail45: the wind law'): a supplied clause, not adopted: a record's content is its direction of travel; (S) a record steps along its content (sphere menu: to x + e_k with probability max(0, s.e_k)/sqrt 3), an occupied target exchanges contents with it, a solid site reflects it or, if the body CAPTURES, keeps it; (C) each bond at rate gamma re-draws its pair of contents uniformly on their momentum class. PROVED: number and momentum conserved by every event with explicit local current and momentum flux; the uniform measure is stationary; product states have mass current (1 - rho) g/sqrt 3 and pressure rho/(3 sqrt 3) (sphere menu), wave speed squared (1 - rho)/9; the second-order momentum flux is sqrt3 Pi_ij = (rho/3) delta_ij + A g_i g_j + B g^2 delta_ij with A = (3/5 - rho)/rho, B = -1/(5 rho); from the second-order flux alone (the INVISCID value) the force of a uniform wind g1 on a body drawing the inflow q is A q g1 = (3/5 - rho)/(1 - rho) times the simple estimate Q2 g1/rho (sign change at rho = 3/5); in free streaming it is exactly the simple estimate, K_0 = sqrt3/(4 pi rho (1 - rho)) in F = K Q1 Q2/r^2. EXECUTED (side 96, gamma 1 unless said): the wind around one capturing body equals sqrt3 Q <1/r^2>/(4 pi (1 - rho)) within 0.974 to 1.003 from r = 7 to 32 with the density flat; two capturing bodies attract with F = K Q1 Q2/r^2, symmetric in the two bodies, K = 0.49 to 0.72 at density 0.3; K/K_0 = 1.02, 1.0, 0.72, 0.57 at density 0.15, 0.3, 0.5, 0.75 (NO sign change) and 1.13, 0.87 at gamma = 0.1, 4: the executed flows have Reynolds numbers below 0.1 and do not follow the inviscid value; the capture rate is NOT the record count for dense bodies (a ball with a tenth of its sites captures 43 per cent of the full ball; Q grows like the square of the radius). Simulators: probes/lib/inertial.py and probes/lib/inertial_bodies.py (see their docstrings); porous bodies need the constructor changed as described in the task. TASK: the executed law's charge is the capture rate Q, which for dense bodies follows the surface. (a) For a porous body (N capturing sites spread at random in a ball of radius R) in the inertial gas at density rho, derive Q(N, R) in the diffusive-transport picture (a gas of mean free path ell: Q = 4 pi D_eff R rho times a function of the opacity N sigma/(R^2) ...): give the crossover N* below which Q is proportional to N and the saturated value. Use the clause's own transport coefficients (derive D_eff for a tagged record from the streaming and scattering rules, or state clearly what is assumed). (b) Predict the executed numbers: R = 5, N = 51, 164, 515 gave Q = 9.4, 17.8, 21.8 at rho = 0.29, gamma = 1; solid balls R = 2, 3, 4, 5 gave 3.2, 7.8, 13.2, 21.8. (c) Conclude: for which bodies is the force proportional to N_1 N_2, and what does additivity cost (how empty must matter be)? check.py: exact capture probability of a single streaming record (no gas) by a small porous body, by enumeration.  DELIVERABLE, in your unit worktree on ai/probes: probes/work/derive/transparent-bodies-capture-rate/<your worker name>/ATTEMPT.md and check.py. ATTEMPT.md: (1) the exact statement you attempt; (2) numbered steps, each marked PROVED (argument given in full), CHECKED (a finite fact check.py verifies exactly) or ASSUMED; (3) if the route fails, the FIRST step that fails and why: a precise no-go for a route is a result; (4) what would finish it. check.py: exact arithmetic (fractions, integers, sympy) for every finite claim; it prints `SUMMARY: PROVED ...`, `SUMMARY: COUNTEREXAMPLE ...`, `SUMMARY: PARTIAL <what is new and exact>` or `SUMMARY: ROUTE FAILS AT <step>`, and a line `HIT: <the claim>` ONLY when you claim a proof, a counterexample, or a new exact partial result others can build on; a HIT is handed to a worker of another model family to referee line by line, so write for a hostile reader. Rules: definitions come from the notes on the PR branches named above (git fetch origin <branch>; git show origin/<branch>:<note>; find them with gh pr view <n> --json files,headRefName); any outside theorem you use must be re-proved at the scope you use it or listed under ASSUMED; no status words (proved theorems are promoted by the supervisor after the referee). Have your own plan BEFORE reading the prior attempts printed at claim time; then either build on a refereed partial result or take a different route. Run: python3 probes/run_probe.py <task> --worker <name> --model <model> --review "..." --extra "python3 probes/work/derive/transparent-bodies-capture-rate/<name>/check.py"
